scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: My laptop (LAPTOP1, on the office WiFi) says it is
connected to the wireless -- full bars -- and yet nothing loads, I cannot
get anywhere at all. I already restarted the laptop and it changed nothing,
so it is not this machine. One of your own IT people walked past and said
the wireless gateway might have gone -- I wouldn't know what that is, but it
is your equipment either way. Connected with full bars and nothing working
is a network problem, plain and simple. Get the wireless actually working
again today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough multi-layer sweep found no network fault. laptop1's Layer 1 through Layer 3 stack is fully healthy: its interface is UP, it holds the correct IP address (10.6.0.100/24) and default gateway (10.6.0.1) for its VLAN 40 segment, and it can successfully ping every other host in the topology — including pc1 (10.1.0.100), pc3 (10.3.0.100), and the DNS server srv1 (10.5.0.4) — all at 0% loss. The "wireless gateway" aswa1 is running normally with all four interfaces UP, the correct VLAN-aware bridge configuration, and PVID 40 correctly assigned to laptop1's port.

The DNS server (srv1) is operational, running BIND with `recursion no` explicitly set in its configuration — a deliberate offline-lab design choice documented in the config comments — and is authoritative only for the `jeremysitlab.com` zone. Queries for external names like google.com receive an immediate REFUSED response from every host in the lab (including pc1), not just laptop1. Internal `jeremysitlab.com` names resolve correctly to 10.5.0.4 from laptop1.

The OSPF routing fabric is healthy across all 32 routes and all adjacencies. No traffic-control shaping, no MAC conflicts, no ACL drops on active traffic, and no resource pressure were detected on any device.

The user's "nothing loads" experience reflects the absence of browsable services in this offline lab — there is no web server running and there is no routed internet path — not a network infrastructure fault. The IT person's theory that the wireless gateway failed is incorrect; aswa1 is fully operational.

Root cause: No anomaly exists; the network infrastructure is functioning as designed for an offline testbed lab with no web services and no internet uplink.

Fix: No corrective action required on the network. If internet or web-service access is needed, a web server and/or an internet-facing NAT/routing configuration must be added to the lab design.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms LAPTOP1 is up and can reach network hosts and that aswa1 is operational, but it does not explicitly state that the keepalived/VRRP master owns the virtual gateway IP (10.6.0.1).

The agent's logs show direct, relevant measurements (interface IPs, pings, ARP, dig responses, named.conf) that support the conclusion that the WLAN and routing fabric are healthy and the observed symptom is due to expected offline-lab DNS/service design. Reasoning is consistent and alternative causes were checked.
